records.question: What is the daily room rent sub-limit under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The daily room rent sub‑limit under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **Rs. 7,500 per day**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: What is the ICU or ICCU daily charges limit under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Under Apex Health Shield Version 2, there is **no sub‑limit** for ICU/ICCU charges – the insurer covers the actual charges up to the Sum Insured. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: How many days of pre-hospitalisation expenses are covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?

records.question: How many days of post-hospitalisation expenses are covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?

records.question: What is the road ambulance limit per hospitalisation under Apex Health Shield Version 2?

records.question: What is the coverage limit for AYUSH treatments under Apex Health Shield Version 2?

records.question: What is the coverage limit for day care procedures under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The coverage limit for day‑care procedures under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is up to the Sum Insured. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: What is the annual limit for organ donor expenses in the benefits table of Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The annual limit for organ donor expenses under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **Rs. 2,00,000 per policy year**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: What is the daily hospital cash allowance and maximum days covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The daily hospital cash allowance under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **Rs. 2,000 per day**, and it is payable for a maximum of **15 days** per admission. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: What waiting period applies to organ donor expenses in the inpatient schedule of Apex Health Shield Version 2?

records.question: What waiting period applies to the daily hospital cash allowance in the inpatient schedule of Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The daily hospital cash allowance has an initial waiting period of **30 days** before it becomes payable. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: What is the initial waiting period for illnesses other than accidental injury under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The initial waiting period for all illnesses other than accidental bodily injury under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: What is the waiting period for cataract surgery under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The waiting period for cataract surgery under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **12 months**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: What is the waiting period for hernia and piles under Apex Health Shield Version 2?

records.question: What is the waiting period for Benign Prostatic Hypertrophy (BPH) under Apex Health Shield Version 2?

records.question: What is the waiting period for joint replacement surgery under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The waiting period for joint replacement surgery (unless accidental) under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **24 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases declared at inception under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The waiting period for pre‑existing diseases declared at inception under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **36 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: What is the monetary capping limit per eye for cataract surgery under Clause 3.4 of Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The monetary capping limit for cataract surgery under Clause 3.4 of Apex Health Shield Version 2 is Rs. 60,000 per eye. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: What are the base Sum Insured options available under Harbor Wellness Silver?
records.answer: The base Sum Insured options available under Harbor Wellness Silver are **Rs. 5 Lakhs** and **Rs. 10 Lakhs**[HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1]

records.question: What are the base Sum Insured options available under Harbor Wellness Gold?

records.question: How often is the annual health check-up covered under Harbor Wellness Silver?

records.question: How often is the annual health check-up covered under Harbor Wellness Gold?

records.question: What is the maximum wellness renewal discount based on steps for Harbor Wellness Silver?

records.question: What is the maximum wellness renewal discount based on steps for Harbor Wellness Gold?

records.question: What is the coverage limit for worldwide emergency cover under Harbor Wellness Gold?

records.question: What room category entitlement is provided under Harbor Wellness Advantage?

records.question: What is the daily ICU charges limit under Harbor Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: There is no daily limit on ICU charges under Harbor Wellness Advantage. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2]

records.question: How many days of pre-hospitalisation expenses are covered under Harbor Wellness Advantage?

records.question: How many days of post-hospitalisation expenses are covered under Harbor Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: Post‑hospitalisation expenses are covered for **180 days after discharge** [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2].

records.question: What is the normal road ambulance coverage limit under Harbor Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: The normal road ambulance coverage limit under Harbor Wellness Advantage is **up to Rs. 5,000 per hospitalisation**[HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2]

records.question: What is the air ambulance limit for the Gold variant under Harbor Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: The air ambulance coverage limit for the Harbor Wellness Advantage Gold variant is up to Rs. 5 Lakhs. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2]

records.question: What is the lump-sum benefit payable for Cancer of Specified Severity under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The lump‑sum benefit payable for Cancer of Specified Severity under the Critical Illness Rider is **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured**[SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].

records.question: What survival period is required to claim for Cancer of Specified Severity under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The survival period required to claim for Cancer of Specified Severity under the Critical Illness Rider is **30 days** [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].

records.question: What benefit is payable for First Heart Attack (Myocardial Infarction) under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The benefit payable for a First Heart Attack (Myocardial Infarction) under the Critical Illness Rider is **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured**[SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1]

records.question: What survival period is required for a First Heart Attack claim under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The survival period required for a First Heart Attack claim under the Critical Illness Rider is 30 days [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].

records.question: What is the lump-sum payout for Open Chest CABG under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The Critical Illness Rider pays a lump‑sum benefit equal to **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured** for an Open Chest CABG diagnosis. [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1]

records.question: What is the benefit payable for Kidney Failure Requiring Dialysis under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The benefit payable for Kidney Failure Requiring Dialysis under the Critical Illness Rider is 100 % of the Rider Sum Insured. [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1]

records.question: What survival period is required for Major Organ or Bone Marrow Transplant under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The survival period required for Major Organ / Bone Marrow Transplant under the Critical Illness Rider is **30 days** [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].

records.question: What is the commission percentage for the Silver tier in the Internal Agent Guide?
records.answer: The commission percentage for the Silver tier is **7%** [AGENT_GUIDE_FAKE p.1].

records.question: How is Inpatient Hospitalisation defined in Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, **Inpatient Hospitalisation** is defined as “admission into a Hospital for a minimum contiguous period of 24 consecutive hours”[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1]

records.question: What is the minimum bed requirement for a Hospital in towns with a population over 10,000 under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The policy defines a hospital in towns with a population of more than 10,000 as an institution that must have at least **15 in‑patient beds** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].

records.question: What is the lookback time window for Pre-existing Disease (PED) diagnosis in Apex Health Shield Version 2 definitions?
records.answer: The lookback time window for a Pre‑existing Disease (PED) diagnosis in Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **36 months prior to policy inception**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].

records.question: What is the duration of the Free-Look Period defined in Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The Free‑Look Period is 15 days from the date of receipt of the policy documents. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5]

records.question: What is the definition of Grace Period under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The Grace Period is defined as the specified period of **30 days immediately following the premium due date during which a payment can be made to maintain policy continuity**. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1]

records.question: Is cosmetic surgery covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Cosmetic surgery is excluded under Apex Health Shield Version 2. The policy states that treatment or surgery for aesthetic reasons, change of appearance, or plastic surgery is not covered unless it is reconstructive surgery following an accidental bodily injury. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: Are claims for self-inflicted injury or suicide attempt payable under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: No. Claims arising from intentional self‑inflicted injury, suicide attempts, or hazardous adventure sports are strictly non‑payable under Apex Health Shield Version 2. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: What maternity benefit coverage is provided under Section 4.3 of Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Section 4.3 of Apex Health Shield Version 2 provides that inpatient medical expenses for maternity—including normal or cesarean delivery—are covered up to Rs. 50,000 per delivery after a waiting period of 24 months, and this benefit is available for up to 2 deliveries. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: Under what condition is dental treatment covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Dental treatment or surgery is covered only when it requires hospitalization that arises **solely from an accidental injury**. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: Are weight loss treatments and bariatric surgery covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Weight‑loss treatments and bariatric surgery are **not covered** under Apex Health Shield Version 2. They are listed as exclusions in the policy. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: Are hospital admissions primarily for diagnostic evaluations covered under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: No. Hospital admissions that are primarily for diagnostic, radiological or laboratory examinations without active inpatient medical treatment are excluded from coverage under Apex Health Shield Version 2. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: How much advance notice is required for planned hospitalisation under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The policy requires that the insured (or their representative) notify the insurer **at least 48 hours before the planned admission** at a network hospital. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5]

records.question: When must notice of emergency hospitalisation be provided under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Notice of an emergency hospitalisation must be given within 24 hours of the emergency admission or before discharge, whichever comes first. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5]

records.question: Within how many days after discharge must claim documents be submitted under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: Claim documents must be submitted within **30 days of discharge** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].

records.question: What mandatory co-payment applies to senior citizens aged 65 and above under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The mandatory co‑payment for senior citizens aged 65 years and above under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **10 % of each admissible claim** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].

records.question: What is the cumulative bonus percentage increase per claim-free year under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The cumulative bonus increases the base Sum Insured by **20 % for each claim‑free policy year** under Apex Health Shield Version 2 [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].

records.question: What is the maximum cumulative bonus limit under Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The maximum cumulative bonus under Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **100 % of the base Sum Insured** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].

records.question: What is the expense limit for living organ donor harvesting under Clause 6.3 of Apex Health Shield Version 2?
records.answer: The expense limit for living organ donor harvesting under Clause 6.3 of Apex Health Shield Version 2 is **Rs. 2,00,000**. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6]

records.question: Does Harbor Wellness Advantage require a co-payment for senior citizens entering the policy?
records.answer: No. Harbor Wellness Advantage offers complete freedom from co‑payments regardless of entry age, so senior citizens are not required to pay a co‑payment when entering the policy. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1]

records.question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases under Harbor Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: The waiting period for pre‑existing diseases under Harbor Wellness Advantage is 36 months of continuous coverage. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.3]

records.question: What is the waiting period and sub-limit for cataract surgery under Harbor Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: The waiting period for cataract surgery under the Harbor Wellness Advantage policy is **24 months**, and the sub‑limit is **Rs. 50,000 per eye** [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.3].

records.question: How can a policyholder cancel their policy during the free-look period under Harbor Wellness Advantage?
records.answer: A policyholder may cancel the Harbor Wellness Advantage policy by sending a written notice within the 15‑day free‑look period that begins on the day the policy is delivered. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.4]

records.question: What is the initial waiting period for the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The initial waiting period for the Critical Illness Rider is **90 days from the policy inception** [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.2].

records.question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing critical conditions under the Critical Illness Rider?
records.answer: The waiting period for pre‑existing critical conditions under the Critical Illness Rider is 48 months. [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.2]

records.question: What additional donor harvesting limit is granted in Endorsement APEX-RIDER-END-2022-09?
records.answer: I do not have enough information in the provided policy documents to answer this question.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what minimum duration defines Inpatient Hospitalisation on Page 1, and what daily room rent limit applies on Page 2?
records.answer:
In Apex Health Shield Version 2, an **Inpatient Hospitalisation** is defined as an admission into a hospital for a minimum contiguous period of **24 consecutive hours** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  
The policy provides a **daily room rent limit of Rs. 7,500 per day** for inpatient stays [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how does the Pre-existing Disease definition time window on Page 1 correspond to the PED waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The definition of a Pre‑existing Disease (PED) in the policy states that any condition, ailment or injury that the insured had signs or symptoms of, was diagnosed, or received medical advice or treatment for **within 36 months prior to policy inception** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  
The waiting period for claims involving a PED is also **36 months** from the policy inception date [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  

Thus, the PED definition’s 36‑month time window directly matches the 36‑month waiting period for pre‑existing diseases declared at inception.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how is Co-payment defined on Page 1, and what specific percentage applies to senior citizens on Page 6?
records.answer:
Co‑payment is defined on Page 1 as a cost‑sharing requirement under which the policyholder bears a specified percentage of the admissible claim amount [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  
On Page 6, the policy states that for insured persons aged 65 years and above the mandatory co‑payment is reduced to **10 % per admissible claim** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the initial waiting period for day care procedures on Page 2 compared to the general initial waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The initial waiting period for day‑care procedures is **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].  
The general initial waiting period for all illnesses (except accidental bodily injury) is also **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]. Thus, the waiting period for day‑care procedures matches the general initial waiting period.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how does the organ donor limit in the benefits table on Page 2 align with the organ donor support clause on Page 6?
records.answer:
In Version 2 the organ‑donor benefit is consistently capped at **Rs. 2,00,000**.  
The benefits table on Page 2 states that “Organ Donor Expenses Covered up to Rs. 2,00,000 per policy year” [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].  
The clause on Page 6 confirms that “Hospitalisation expenses incurred for organ donation harvesting from a living donor are payable up to an enhanced limit of Rs. 2,00,000” [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].  

Thus, the organ‑donor limit in the benefits table aligns exactly with the organ‑donor support clause, both setting the same monetary ceiling of Rs. 2,00,000.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the cataract surgery waiting period in the table on Page 3, and what sub-limit is specified in Clause 3.4 on Page 3 and Page 2?
records.answer:
In Apex Health Shield Version 2, the cataract surgery waiting period listed in the table on Page 3 is **12 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  
Clause 3.4 on Page 3 specifies a cataract sub‑limit of **Rs. 60,000 per eye** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  

Page 2 of the policy does not contain Clause 3.4 or any mention of a cataract sub‑limit.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, how does the accidental bodily injury exception to the waiting period on Page 3 relate to the reconstructive cosmetic surgery clause on Page 4?
records.answer:
In the policy, the 30‑day waiting period that applies to “all illnesses” is **not** applied to claims that arise from accidental bodily injury[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  
The cosmetic‑surgery exclusion on page 4 states that cosmetic or aesthetic surgery is excluded **unless** it is a reconstructive procedure performed after an accidental bodily injury[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].  

Thus, when a reconstructive cosmetic surgery is performed following an accidental bodily injury, it is covered immediately (no 30‑day waiting period) because the injury itself is exempt from the general waiting period.

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the maternity benefit waiting period under Section 4.3 on Page 4 compared to the general initial waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The maternity benefit under Section 4.3 of Apex Health Shield Version 2 has a waiting period of **24 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].  
By contrast, the general initial waiting period for all illnesses (except accidental bodily injury) is **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what notice is required for planned admission on Page 5, and what minimum hospital stay is required on Page 1?
records.answer:
The policy requires that for a planned admission the insured (or their representative) must give notice to the insurer **at least 48 hours before the scheduled admission** at a network hospital [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].  

The policy defines an inpatient hospitalisation as an admission that lasts a **minimum of 24 consecutive hours** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].

records.question: In Apex Health Shield Version 2, what is the Free-Look Period duration defined on Page 1, and what refund terms apply under Section 5.3 on Page 5?
records.answer:
The Free‑Look Period is **15 days** from the date the policyholder receives the policy documents [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  

Under Section 5.3 (Page 5), the policy allows a 15‑day free‑look period from the date of physical or electronic receipt of the policy schedule. If no claim is made during that period, the premium is refunded **subject to minimal administrative charges** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].

records.question: In Harbor Wellness Advantage, what Sum Insured options are offered for Gold on Page 1, and what room category entitlement applies on Page 2?
records.answer:
Harbor Wellness Advantage – Gold Sum‑Insured options (Page 1): Rs. 25 Lakhs and Rs. 50 Lakhs [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1].  

Room‑category entitlement (Page 2): Single Private Room (up to the Sum Insured) with no room‑rent capping [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2].

records.question: In Harbor Wellness Advantage, what worldwide emergency coverage is provided for Gold on Page 1, and what air ambulance limit is provided on Page 2?
records.answer:
The Harbor Wellness Advantage Gold plan includes worldwide emergency coverage of up to **$50,000**[HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1].  
For air ambulance services, the Gold plan provides a limit of **up to 5 Lakhs**[HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2].

records.question: In Harbor Wellness Advantage, how does the free co-payment highlight on Page 1 compare to the pre-existing disease waiting period on Page 3?
records.answer:
The brochure on Page 1 emphasizes that **Harbor Wellness Advantage offers “complete freedom from co‑payments regardless of entry age,”** meaning that policyholders pay no co‑payment from the first day of coverage.  
In contrast, the waiting‑period clause on Page 3 states that **pre‑existing diseases are only covered after 36 months of continuous coverage**.  

Thus, while the free‑co‑payment feature provides immediate, cost‑free access to care, the pre‑existing disease waiting period requires a three‑year waiting period before such conditions are covered.  

[HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1] [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.3]

records.question: How does the daily room rent sub-limit compare between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer:
In Apex Health Shield Version 1 the daily room‑rent sub‑limit is **Rs. 5,000 per day** [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2].  
In Version 2 this allowance has been increased to **Rs. 7,500 per day** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: How do the ICU charges limits differ between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer:
In Version 1 of the Apex Health Shield, ICU/ICCU charges are capped at a sub‑limit of **Rs. 10,000 per day** [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2].  
In Version 2, the policy removes that sub‑limit, allowing coverage of **actual ICU/ICCU charges up to the Sum Insured** with no daily cap [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: How does pre-hospitalisation expense coverage duration compare between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer:
Pre‑hospitalisation cover in Version 1 of the Apex Health Shield policy extends **30 days prior to admission** [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2].  
In Version 2, this period is doubled to **60 days prior to admission** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: How does post-hospitalisation expense coverage duration compare between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer: Post‑hospitalisation coverage lasts **60 days after discharge in Version 1** of the Apex Health Shield policy, whereas in **Version 2 it extends to 90 days after discharge** [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2][APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: How does the road ambulance limit per hospitalisation compare between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer:
The road ambulance limit per hospitalisation is higher in Version 2.  
- Version 1 provides a limit of **Rs. 2,000** per hospitalisation [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2].  
- Version 2 increases this limit to **Rs. 3,500** per hospitalisation [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: How did the waiting period for cataract surgery change from Version 1 to Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer: The waiting period for cataract surgery was reduced from 24 months in Version 1 to 12 months in Version 2 of the Apex Health Shield policy. [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.3] [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: How did the cataract surgery monetary sub-limit per eye change between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer: The cataract surgery sub‑limit per eye was raised from **Rs. 40,000** in Version 1 to **Rs. 60,000** in Version 2 of the Apex Health Shield policy. [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.3] [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: Which version of Apex Health Shield has a shorter waiting period for pre-existing diseases declared at inception?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield Version 2 (2024 Revised) has the shorter waiting period for pre‑existing diseases declared at inception, with a waiting period of 36 months compared to 48 months in Version 1 [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3] [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.3].

records.question: Do both Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield cover maternity expenses, and how do they differ?
records.answer:
Version 1 of the Apex Health Shield policy does **not** cover maternity expenses.  
In Version 1, maternity and childbirth are listed as exclusions under Section 4.3 [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.4].

Version 2 of the policy **does** cover maternity expenses.  
Under Version 2, inpatient medical expenses for maternity and normal or cesarean delivery are covered up to Rs. 50,000 per delivery, after a waiting period of 24 months, and this benefit is available for up to two deliveries [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].

records.question: How did the mandatory co-payment for senior citizens aged 65 and above change between Version 1 and Version 2 of Apex Health Shield?
records.answer:
The mandatory co‑payment for senior citizens (aged 65 years and above) was reduced from **20 % of each admissible claim in Version 1** to **10 % of each admissible claim in Version 2**.  
[APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.6] [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6]
